title: Composite Duct Segment in the Thrust Reverser Cascade Box Assembly
abstract: Replacing the aluminium duct segment in the cascade box assembly with a moulded composite item is proposed to save mass and to remove the corrosion findings that dominate reverser shop visits.

sections.reason: Cascade box shop visits are dominated by two findings: corrosion of the aluminium duct segment where it meets the drain path, and impact damage at the same station from ground handling around the reverser. Eighteen segments were scrapped across the fleet in two years, all for corrosion rather than fatigue. A moulded composite segment removes the corrosion mechanism entirely and, on the supplier estimate, saves 4.2 kg per engine. Fuel burn is a secondary but real driver on a component this far outboard.
sections.description: The aluminium duct segment is replaced by a moulded composite item with a co-cured erosion strip on the leading face and metallic inserts at the two attachment stations. The reverser actuation duct D7830121464250 is retained but its clamp interface is re-machined to suit the composite wall thickness, and the reverser clamp set AS815197-77 is replaced by a wider-footprint item to spread the clamping load. Work is in the reverser and pylon inboard areas, zones 481, 483 and 433, with the reverser opened on its hinges. The cascade duct fitting 22ET is refitted unchanged and the cascade seal 4056ET is renewed as a matter of course. No change is made to the cascade vanes, to the translating sleeve or to the actuation system.
sections.effects: Estimated mass reduction of 4.2 kg per engine, giving a small but measurable cruise fuel benefit on long sectors. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: the clamp footprint and the wall thickness both change and a mixed installation would leave the clamping load unbalanced. The corrosion inspection at reverser shop visit is deleted for post-modification assemblies, and a tap test for disbond is introduced in its place. Repair philosophy changes from metallic blend-out to a composite repair scheme, which the repair design office has to write.
sections.embodiment_note: Production and spares. No retrofit campaign is proposed: the segment is a shop-replaceable item and operators will migrate as assemblies come through overhaul. A production cut-in date has not been set because the composite supplier has not yet been selected.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm that the composite segment tolerates the bleed duct thermal environment at the inboard station, and whether the reverser fire zone statement needs re-issuing for a non-metallic component in that position.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in date not set, gated by composite supplier selection
